$comment: Settings schema for the OptiScaler-FFXIV fork: the machine-readable reference of fork ini keys. One entry per key; adding a key later is one local entry here. tools/gen-settings.ps1 reads this file and writes docs/SETTINGS.md; -Check mode verifies the committed file is up to date. Format vocabularies: type = bool|int|float|enum|string; applies = live (menu change applies at once) | restart (game restart) | start (read once at start); menu = {tab, card} of OptiScaler/ext/core/MenuLayout.h, or iniOnly with the reason (those keys are also listed in kIniOnlyKeys of OptiScaler/ext/core/MenuManifest.h). Every new key defaults to today's behaviour (default auto).

keys.name: Mode
keys.description: HUD-less frame generation (DLSS-G): keep the HUD sharp in fast camera motion. FFXIV only. off = today's behaviour; recomposition = DLSS-G recomposes the UI itself (switching to or from it recreates DLSS-G: frame generation restarts for a moment), recommended with [DLSSG] RenderPreset = auto; ui_free = frame generation runs on the UI-free image and the UI is pasted back at the real frame rate; experimental, and the micro-stutter seen while the coverage guard was tripped was gone with the default probe interval of 8 in one play session on 2026-10-31 with DLSS-G render preset C (at 1 it came back). Any other value counts as off.

keys.name: MaskThreshold
keys.description: Advanced: largest per-channel difference (0..1) between the final and the UI-free frame that still counts as the same pixel.

keys.name: MaskDilation
keys.description: Advanced: grow the detected UI area by this many pixels.

keys.name: PasteCleanup
keys.description: Advanced: also paste where the previous frame had UI and this one does not (clears the ghost of UI that just closed).

keys.name: SteadyTiming
keys.description: Advanced: paste the UI of one real frame behind (steadier world-anchored UI, slightly older).

keys.name: CoverageGuard
keys.description: Advanced: fall back to normal frame generation when more than this share (0..1) of the pixels is flagged as UI for 5 measurements in a row (full-screen fades, a ReShade preset before the capture). 0 = off. While fallen back the UI-free image keeps being measured, and the guard returns after 30 measurements in a row at or below 0.75x this value, or after 120 presents with no new measurement.

keys.name: ShowDetectedUi
keys.description: Debug: tint the pasted UI area.

keys.name: ReShadePresets
keys.defaultMeans: auto (on when a ReShade runtime with an enabled technique registered)
keys.description: Apply ReShade presets in place at the UI boundary, so the UI-free image has them and the HUD stays unfiltered. auto = when ReShade registered a runtime and at least one technique is enabled; on = always try; off = never. Switching to off applies at once; switching back to on after the game started with off needs a restart.

keys.name: GuardMode

menu.iniOnly: opt-in guard policy not tried in a game: kept out of the menu until it has been

keys.description: Developer switch, ini only: how the coverage guard trips and releases. legacy = as described under CoverageGuard. density = trips when 3 of the last 12 measurements are over the limit, returns only after 60 measurements in a row at or below 0.75 x the limit. Any other value counts as legacy.

keys.name: GuardReleaseHolds

menu.iniOnly: opt-in time limit of the density guard, which has not been tried in a game

keys.description: Developer switch, ini only, density guard only: 0 = off. With N above 0 the guard leaves the fallback after N anchor-later frames in a row whose window had at least one measurement and none over the release level (a window without one counts neither way), even though the 60-measurement clean run cannot complete while they keep coming. The guard trips again by the normal rule.

keys.name: GuardTripOnAnchorLater

menu.iniOnly: opt-in per-frame trip of the density guard, which has not been tried in a game

keys.description: Developer switch, ini only, density guard only: a frame the game anchored after off-screen UI draws trips the guard at once, so the base of that very frame is not swapped, instead of waiting about two presents for its measurement. The trip then ends by the normal release rules.

keys.name: ProbeInterval
keys.defaultMeans: 8 (one present in eight while falling back; 1 = every present, the behaviour before this key)
keys.description: Advanced, experimental: while the coverage guard is tripped (falling back), build the UI-free capture and its mask on only one present in this many; the others are plain frame generation. The boundary still applies the ReShade presets in the same place on every frame. The guard then comes back after about 30 x this many presents of a clean scene instead of 30. 1 = every present. Building them on every present is the suspected cause of the micro-stutter seen while falling back (with DLSS-G render preset C; felt in play, not measured): in one play session on 2026-10-31, 8 removed that stutter and 1 brought it back. Only that session and preset were compared. Unit-tested.

keys.name: ProbeAbSeconds

menu.iniOnly: developer A/B of the probe interval: a menu control would show the player which block runs

keys.description: Developer switch, ini only: a blind A/B of ProbeInterval. With N above 0 the engine alternates between measuring on every present and on one present in ProbeInterval, in blocks of N seconds (each pair of blocks holds one of each, in an order drawn at start) and logs one line per block. 0 = off; nothing happens while ProbeInterval is 1.

keys.name: AnchorRule
keys.description: Advanced, experimental: where the UI-free image is taken on a frame whose first interface draw after the scene goes to an off-screen target (a small interface target drawn before the HUD in the world, probably the minimap). r1b = at the first interface draw into the backbuffer; early = at that off-screen draw, by copying the backbuffer there, before the off-screen block and the draws that follow it. Frames whose first interface draw goes to the backbuffer do not change; a frame with ReShade presets to apply at the UI boundary keeps r1b. Both HUD-less modes use this image; the coverage guard runs only in ui_free, so in recomposition a wrong early image goes to DLSS-G unchecked (only its size and format are checked). Any other value counts as r1b. Unit-tested, not tried in a game.

keys.name: HdrPaste

menu.iniOnly: opt-in for a GPU path no HDR user has confirmed yet: kept out of the menu until one does

keys.description: Developer switch, ini only: with HDR output and Mode = ui_free, make the paste's HDR stage before the first paste image. Without it that image is never built and ui_free stays on normal frame generation under HDR output.

keys.name: Diagnostics

menu.iniOnly: shows the HUD-less diagnostics card of the FFXIV tab; observation only

keys.description: Developer gate, ini only: switch on the game-side UI boundary detector's observation (draw tracking and the shader registry), show the HUD-less diagnostics card of the FFXIV tab and turn on the ReShade add-on probe. Observation only, it does not change the frame. Set it before the game starts.

keys.name: ReShadeProbe

menu.iniOnly: shows the ReShade add-on probe card

keys.description: Developer gate, ini only: the ReShade add-on also subscribes to the effect-runtime events, writes reshade-probe.txt and shows the diagnostics card. Set it before the game starts.

keys.name: PlateDiagnostics

menu.iniOnly: developer probes (log only) of the output stream and the UI draws

keys.description: Developer switch, ini only: log-only probes measuring what frame generation delivers and which UI draws could be nameplates. Output goes to OptiScaler/plate-probe/<run>/. Nothing in the frame changes. Set it before the game starts.

keys.name: PlateInterp
keys.description: Native nameplates: take the game's own nameplate draws out of the frame and draw them back over every output frame. off = today's behaviour; endpoint = drawn back unchanged, which proves the path and leaves the picture the same as with the key off; on = accepted for the next stage (this build has no plate tracker, so on draws exactly what endpoint draws and moves nothing). DLSS-G with a multiplier of 2 or more and SDR output only; any doubt keeps the plates native.

keys.name: PlatePhaseOffset
keys.defaultMeans: auto (1: generated frames first, the real frame last)
keys.description: Advanced, for the plate tracker stage: which output of a batch shows the older plate position, as the constant of the per-output share. No effect in this build (no plate tracker yet).

keys.name: PlateMaxStep
keys.description: Advanced, for the plate tracker stage: the largest distance a nameplate may be moved between two outputs, in output pixels; a plate that moves further is drawn unshifted for that frame. No effect in this build (no plate tracker yet).

keys.name: FfxivHDR
keys.description: OptiHDR (FFXIV): HDR10 output for the D3D11 game through the DX12 presenter. Needs Windows HDR enabled on the game display before launch, and works with DLSS-G, XeFG, or with frame generation off. Restart after changing.

keys.name: Mode
keys.description: 0 = SDR expansion (the game's SDR image is expanded to HDR10), 1 = scene HDR (the game's tonemap stages are replayed in FP16 next to the SDR chain; the SDR chain, ReShade and the HUD are untouched).

keys.name: PeakNits
keys.description: Peak brightness of the HDR output, in nits.

keys.name: PaperWhiteNits
keys.description: Paper-white brightness of the HDR output, in nits. Never above PeakNits.

keys.name: HighlightExpansion
keys.description: Mode 0: how far above paper white the SDR highlights are expanded (0 = none, 1 = up to PeakNits).

keys.name: Contrast
keys.description: Output grading applied before PQ encoding: contrast.

keys.name: Saturation
keys.description: Output grading applied before PQ encoding: saturation.

keys.name: Vibrance
keys.description: Output grading applied before PQ encoding: vibrance.

keys.name: NRSceneInput
keys.description: Mode 1: run NR on the linear HDR scene instead of the SDR colour. Experimental. Needs NR before upscaling or PreSR.

keys.name: DLSSSceneInput
keys.description: Feed native scene HDR through DLSS w/Dx12 before SDR ReShade processing. Experimental; enable RenoDX scene HDR and restart after changing.

keys.name: ScreenshotKey
keys.description: Optional screenshot key (Windows virtual-key code). -1 leaves it unbound.

keys.name: ScreenshotFormat
keys.description: Save one PNG: 0 = SDR for sharing (default), 1 = HDR. Requires OptiHDR active.

keys.name: ScreenshotIccOnly
keys.description: Use BT.2100 PQ ICC metadata without an outer PNG cICP chunk for HDR sharing. HDR pixel values are preserved. Viewer compatibility varies.

keys.name: ScreenshotMenu
keys.description: HDR PNG only: while the menu is open, capture the presented image after the menu was drawn onto it, including its HDR colours. Needs the overlay menu; SDR captures are unchanged.

keys.name: PreviewNRTrace
keys.description: Rate-limited trace log lines for the character preview path (finisher verdicts, evaluations, UI swaps). Only logs, changes nothing.

keys.name: ReShadeHighlights
keys.description: Mode 1: preserve measured scene highlights through ReShade's grading (experimental).

keys.name: UiExpansion
keys.description: Mode 1 interface curve: how far above paper white the interface expands. Follows HighlightExpansion when left on auto; a number overrides it for the interface only. Read by the continuous composition only; the legacy composition keeps using HighlightExpansion.

keys.name: LegacyComposition

menu.iniOnly: experimental rollback of the scene HDR composition: kept out of the menu until confirmed in a game

keys.description: Mode 1 composition: true keeps the two-rule composition of tagged previews and the colour band; false selects the continuous composition of world and interface light. Experimental, will become the default after in-game confirmation.

keys.name: Enabled
keys.description: Neural Rendering (the DLSS NR model) on the upscaled frame (ordinary super resolution, or super resolution combined with ray reconstruction), before frame generation sees it. Needs an installed NR runtime; undocumented and driven directly, so none of it is officially supported.

keys.name: WorkingScale
keys.description: What fraction of the frame the model works at. The frame itself is never reduced: only the model's own work is done small and enlarged. Cost falls with the square of this. Above 1.0 (DX12 and Vulkan) the model supersamples. ScaleUpKey and ScaleDownKey move it live between 25% and 200% (5% per press; only the uniform WorkingScale moves); TransferToggleKey flips the enlargement mode. All three hotkeys are unbound by default.

keys.name: WorkingScaleX
keys.description: A different model resolution per axis (DX12 only): the fraction of the frame width the model works at. Valid values are 0 (follows WorkingScale) or 0.25 to 2. Cost falls with the product of the two axes.

keys.name: WorkingScaleY
keys.description: A different model resolution per axis (DX12 only): the fraction of the frame height the model works at. Valid values are 0 (follows WorkingScale) or 0.25 to 2. Cost falls with the product of the two axes.

keys.name: Passes
keys.description: Number of sequential model layers between one encode and one final composition. 1 is normal; 2 and 3 cost almost exactly 2x and 3x the model time. Values are clamped to 1..3 (up to 30 with UnlockPasses on).

keys.name: Intensity
keys.description: How strongly each model pass edits the frame, for ordinary super resolution and combined ray reconstruction + super resolution. Pass 2 and 3 inherit pass 1 when left on auto.

keys.name: Transfer
keys.description: How a reduced-resolution model result is enlarged. 0 enlarges the complete model output; 1 enlarges only its matched residual. No effect at WorkingScale 1.0 or above.

keys.name: TransferStrength
keys.description: How far the frame moves toward the model's picture. 0 gives back exactly what the upscaler produced, 1 is the model's picture, and above 1 carries on past it.

keys.name: RunBeforeSR
keys.description: Run NR before ordinary super resolution on the active colour input instead of after it. Both use WorkingScale and Passes. Before RR, NR processes noisy ray-traced colour: visual results need testing.

keys.name: DepthAwareResolve
keys.description: Depth-aware enlargement of a reduced model (DX12 only): weight each tap of the enlargement filter by how close the game's depth under it is to the depth under the output pixel, so the answer stops at object edges. Nothing at model resolution 100% or above, or while spatial compression is active.

keys.name: ClassicSharpen
keys.description: Sharpens the frame after the Classic enlargement (DX12 only), with an RCAS-style adaptive sharpen ported from upstream's RCAS. Only while the Classic enlargement applies: the model is reduced on some axis and above 100% on none, and the enlargement mode is not Matched residual. Debug views are never sharpened.

keys.name: ClassicSharpenStrength
keys.description: Strength of the Classic sharpening, 0 to 1 (0.4 is upstream RCAS's own default). 0 skips the step entirely; a value that cannot be read falls back to 0.4.

keys.name: Governor
keys.description: Frame-rate governor (experimental): steps the model resolution over 100/90/80/70/60/50% to hold the target frame rate. A run-time cap only: Model resolution stays the ceiling and is never written. Steps down after 3 s below 95% of the target; probes one tier up after 10 s at or above 97% of the target and keeps the probe only if the rate holds 97% of the target over the next 2 s. Stands down while AutoMFG, a per-axis model size or spatial compression is on. A frame-generation feature that reports itself active without an observed count is waited for 2 s at most; past that the present rate is used and the status line says so.

keys.name: GovernorTargetFps
keys.description: Frame rate the governor holds, in frames per second as displayed (frame generation included). 0 is auto: the lower of the frame rate limit and the display refresh rate. Manual values below 30 are raised to 30.

keys.name: GovernorProbe

menu.iniOnly: developer probe: logs once per model build whether a below-created-size evaluate exists; the governor never uses it

keys.description: Developer probe: once per model build, logs whether the model can evaluate below the size it was created for (works / refused / not available). Changes nothing on screen; the governor never uses it.

keys.name: DisableOnFocusLoss
keys.description: Experimental: pause NR while the game window is not the foreground window or is minimised, and resume with a clean history when the window is focused again. Does not change Enabled. Native Vulkan is not paused.

keys.name: SpatialCompression
keys.description: Experimental spatial compression of the model's work area (100% of the frame or less). Which profile it drives is SpatialProfile.

keys.name: SpatialProfile
keys.description: Which profile SpatialCompression drives: 0 Peripheral, 1 Foveated (a full-density centre of FoveaWidth x FoveaHeight pixels easing off over FoveaFalloff to FoveaEdgeX / FoveaEdgeY of the density). NR returns to the ordinary size by itself when the saving would be under 5%.

keys.name: ApplyModel
keys.description: Whether the model's edit is applied. Off keeps the pass running (so HoldFrame works) but shows the clean upscaler frame.

keys.name: Runtime
keys.description: Which NR model file runs. Leave on auto (or empty) for the newest installed, legacy for the old search, or a folder name such as NR.310.9. Changed live from the card; not part of the saved presets.

keys.name: Precision
keys.description: 0 = NVIDIA FP8 (default), 4 = experimental NVFP4 hybrid (coerced to {0,4} on load).

keys.name: DeferredDLSS
keys.description: Experimental: generate NR before SR, upscale its signed contribution with a private DLSS feature and apply it after SR. Takes precedence over RunBeforeSR. Requires a working DLSS SR runtime.

keys.name: PreSRTrailGuard
keys.description: Experimental current-frame bounds for the private PreSR contribution. Live toggle.

keys.name: SplitFrameWork
keys.description: Experimental alternating NR scheduling: NR on A, private SR/FG on B. Adds one more rendered frame of scene buffering.

keys.name: ResidualFG
keys.description: Experimental every-other-frame NR with NVIDIA FG on the residual layer. Delays SR colour one frame.

keys.name: ResidualFGApproxCamera
keys.description: Explicit consent to approximate camera transforms when full camera guides are absent.

keys.name: ToggleKey
keys.description: Virtual-key code toggling the pass in game. Unbound by default; set it from the Keybinds section of the overlay; -1 leaves it unbound.

keys.name: ScaleUpKey
keys.description: Virtual-key code raising the working size by 5% per press (25% to 200%). Only the uniform WorkingScale moves; -1 leaves it unbound.

keys.name: ScaleDownKey
keys.description: Virtual-key code lowering the working size by 5% per press (25% to 200%). Only the uniform WorkingScale moves; -1 leaves it unbound.

keys.name: TransferToggleKey
keys.description: Virtual-key code flipping the enlargement mode (Classic/Matched residual) in game. Does nothing while the Enlargement combo is greyed out; -1 leaves it unbound.

keys.name: ColourStrength
keys.description: Whether the model's colour arrives with its light. 0 keeps the game's own hue exactly; 1 brings the model's colour as well.

keys.name: MaxRatio
keys.description: The most the pass may brighten any pixel, as a multiple. Darkening is not capped.

keys.name: DebugView
keys.description: 0 off, 1 the picture the model sees, 2 its raw answer, 3 what it changed, amplified.

keys.name: Compare
keys.description: Side-by-side / wipe comparison of the pass against itself: 0 off, 1 side by side, 2 wipe.

keys.name: CompareSplit
keys.description: Wipe position for Compare = 2 (0..1).

keys.name: CompareZoom
keys.description: Compare zoom: 1 fits the frame in each half, 2 fills it. Side by side only.

keys.name: CompareSwap
keys.description: Which side the edited frame sits on in a comparison.

keys.name: CompareTags
keys.description: Labels drawn onto the two sides of a comparison.

keys.name: TagScale
keys.description: Size of the comparison labels.

keys.name: SpatialCenterX
keys.description: Spatial compression curve centre, percent (Peripheral profile only).

keys.name: SpatialCenterY
keys.description: Spatial compression curve centre, percent (Peripheral profile only).

keys.name: SpatialWorkX
keys.description: Spatial compression work area, percent (Peripheral profile only).

keys.name: SpatialWorkY
keys.description: Spatial compression work area, percent (Peripheral profile only).

keys.name: SpatialOffsetX
keys.description: Spatial placement offset; the Foveated profile uses it for placement.

keys.name: SpatialOffsetY
keys.description: Spatial placement offset; the Foveated profile uses it for placement.

keys.name: SpatialShiftX
keys.description: Spatial shift (Peripheral profile only).

keys.name: SpatialShiftY
keys.description: Spatial shift (Peripheral profile only).

keys.name: FoveaWidth
keys.description: Foveated full-density centre width, output pixels (clamped to the frame every frame).

keys.name: FoveaHeight
keys.description: Foveated full-density centre height, output pixels (clamped to the frame every frame).

keys.name: FoveaFalloff
keys.description: Foveated falloff length, output pixels (clamped to the frame every frame).

keys.name: FoveaEdgeX
keys.description: Foveated edge density on X (0.25..1).

keys.name: FoveaEdgeY
keys.description: Foveated edge density on Y (0.25..1).

keys.name: PassFeedback
keys.description: Spatial feedback between passes: 1 keeps the raw interpass output, below 1 gamut-bounds the edit and blends it back toward the preceding input.

keys.name: VitEvery
keys.description: Run the bottleneck on every Nth NR evaluation, 1..2. With VitFirstPassOnly only pass 1 is affected.

keys.name: VitAllowUnverified
keys.description: Experimental bottleneck reuse override for alternate runtimes. Bypasses only the module fingerprint check. Incompatible runtimes can corrupt or crash.

keys.name: VitCapture
keys.description: Profiling aid: records the CUDA launches of the first NR evaluations and dumps the ViT module. Never changes a launch. Set it before the game starts.

keys.name: ReplayCapture

menu.iniOnly: developer key: the capture triggers write a full replay set of the pass

keys.description: Developer tool: while on, a capture trigger (the dlssnr-capture.trigger file or AutoCapture) records a replay set of the NR pass (two frames, every dispatch with its inputs and outputs) instead of the before/after frames, for checking shader changes without the game. A capture shows the player's screen: never share it.

keys.name: VitFirstPassOnly
keys.description: Restrict bottleneck reuse to pass 1; later passes compute fully. Set false to restore reuse on every pass. Requires VitEvery=2.

keys.name: ScalingDownscaler
keys.description: Downscaler averaging the model's answer back to native when supersampling. 0 FSR1, 1 Bicubic, 2 CatmullRom, 3 Lanczos2, 4 Lanczos3, 5 Kaiser2, 6 Kaiser3, 7 MAGIC.

keys.name: AutoCapture
keys.description: Write one set of matched before/after frames per session after the capture delay (180 frames). No capture when off.

keys.name: ScanExposure
keys.description: Run the exposure scan even when WhitePointSource is not 2 (developer override).

keys.name: WhitePointSource
keys.defaultMeans: 1 (the exposure the game hands the upscaler)
keys.description: Where the white point comes from: 0 paper white slider, 1 exposure the game hands the upscaler, 2 scanned exposure. Linear buffers only.

keys.name: WhitePointScale
keys.description: Multiplies the white point before the encode (the paper-white control).

keys.name: WhitePointTrim
keys.description: Trim on an exposure-derived white point, kept apart from the manual divisor. 1.0 takes the game's exposure exactly.

keys.name: ScanTrim
keys.description: Trim on the scanned white point (WhitePointSource=2).

keys.name: ScanAnchors
keys.description: Scan calibration table, scan:white;scan:white;... ascending, written by the overlay's anchor buttons. Empty means no anchors.

keys.name: ScanInverted
keys.description: Whether the scan's number rises (false) or falls (true) with the light.

keys.name: ScanMeter
keys.description: Overlay lamp showing what the scan currently thinks the light is doing.

keys.name: LightingHistory
keys.description: FFXIV native scanned lighting: reset NR history on abrupt tone changes. Needs WhitePointSource=2 and a fresh verified scan.

keys.name: Preset
keys.description: Model profile baked into the feature: changing it causes a guarded feature rebuild. Values undocumented; not the SR/RR preset scale.

keys.name: Style
keys.description: Model style baked into the feature: 0 standard, 1 natural, 2 cinematic. Changing it causes a guarded feature rebuild.

keys.name: LocalStructure
keys.description: Local structure strength of the model (pass 1; passes 2 and 3 inherit it when left on auto).

keys.name: LocalTone
keys.description: Local tone strength of the model (pass 1; passes 2 and 3 inherit it when left on auto).

keys.name: SkinStructure
keys.description: -1 means follow local structure (the model's own default, not zero).

keys.name: AutoMask
keys.description: Automatic masking of the model's edit in the final composition.

keys.name: SkinProtection
keys.description: Optional colour-based final-edit filter (not NVIDIA's semantic auto mask). Preview before relying on it.

keys.name: SkinToneEnabled
keys.description: Whether the model's skin-tone handling applies.

keys.name: SkinDetail
keys.description: Skin detail strength of the model.

keys.name: SkinColour
keys.description: Skin colour strength of the model.

keys.name: EnvironmentDetail
keys.description: Environment detail strength of the model.

keys.name: EnvironmentColour
keys.description: Environment colour strength of the model.

keys.name: ShowSkinMask
keys.description: Show the skin mask (debug view of what the skin handling sees).

keys.name: UnlockPasses
keys.description: Optional extended range up to 30 passes. Normal ceiling remains 3; no extra work while off.

keys.name: ReversibleMode
keys.description: RenoDX reversible proxy mode: 0 soft-knee encode and our composition, 1/2 Neutwo composed/replace, 3/4 hybrid composed/replace, 5 linear light and composed.

keys.name: HoldFrame
keys.description: Freeze the NR pass's input so a live setting change re-renders the same frame.

keys.name: Pass2Preset
keys.description: Pass 2 override of the model profile (preset 0..3). Inherits pass 1 when left on auto.

keys.name: Pass2Style
keys.description: Pass 2 override of the model style (0 standard, 1 natural, 2 cinematic). Inherits pass 1 when left on auto.

keys.name: Pass2Intensity
keys.description: Pass 2 override of the model strength. Inherits pass 1 when left on auto.

keys.name: Pass2LocalStructure
keys.description: Pass 2 override of the local structure strength. Inherits pass 1 when left on auto.

keys.name: Pass2LocalTone
keys.description: Pass 2 override of the local tone strength. Auto keeps the legacy later-pass value 0.

keys.name: Pass2SkinStructure
keys.description: Pass 2 override of the skin structure (-1 follows structure). Inherits pass 1 when left on auto.

keys.name: Pass2AutoMask
keys.description: Pass 2 override of the automatic masking. Inherits pass 1 when left on auto.

keys.name: Pass3Preset
keys.description: Pass 3 override of the model profile (preset 0..3). Inherits pass 1 when left on auto.

keys.name: Pass3Style
keys.description: Pass 3 override of the model style (0 standard, 1 natural, 2 cinematic). Inherits pass 1 when left on auto.

keys.name: Pass3Intensity
keys.description: Pass 3 override of the model strength. Inherits pass 1 when left on auto.

keys.name: Pass3LocalStructure
keys.description: Pass 3 override of the local structure strength. Inherits pass 1 when left on auto.

keys.name: Pass3LocalTone
keys.description: Pass 3 override of the local tone strength. Auto keeps the legacy later-pass value 0.

keys.name: Pass3SkinStructure
keys.description: Pass 3 override of the skin structure (-1 follows structure). Inherits pass 1 when left on auto.

keys.name: Pass3AutoMask
keys.description: Pass 3 override of the automatic masking. Inherits pass 1 when left on auto.

keys.name: Trace
keys.defaultMeans: auto (off at the normal log level; on only with file logging at Debug or Trace)

menu.iniOnly: diagnostic switch of the frame-pacing CPU trace

keys.description: Frame pacing trace: every 10 seconds, for each thread and place, one log line with call counts and CPU times. true = on at any log level, false = off, auto = on only with file logging at Debug or Trace. Runs only in FFXIV.

keys.name: GpuTimers
keys.defaultMeans: auto (off unless the trace above is on)

menu.iniOnly: diagnostic switch of the frame-pacing GPU stage timers

keys.description: GPU stage timers: sampled frames time the present copy-in, the ReShade effects and the D3D12 interop copy (true = on at any log level, false = off, auto = on only together with the trace). The interop line also carries a cpu offset in ms, the same samples placed on the CPU clock with the queue's own clock calibration (D3D11 has no such pairing). A timer never waits on the frame path. Add GpuTimers=true for a measurement run with Trace=true.

keys.name: HiddenPresentDoNotWait

menu.iniOnly: debug switch of the hidden DX11 present, compared with the trace

keys.description: The auxiliary present on the hidden swapchain gets DXGI_PRESENT_DO_NOT_WAIT and a busy chain skips that present instead of blocking. Off = exactly the old call.

keys.name: FgRecorder
keys.description: FG event recorder: one JSONL file per session in fg-recordings beside the DLL (presents with HRESULT, Reflex sleeps, AutoMFG lines, NR rebuilds, provider events). Bounded queue, rotation at 16 MiB keeping 9 files per session (144 MiB plus the one queue batch that crossed the limit, about 40 minutes at 60 base fps and 2x frame generation, so a 25-minute session keeps its beginning) and only the newest 5 sessions; off means no thread and no file.

keys.name: FgRecorderMarkKey
keys.description: Virtual-key code of the recorder's one-key mark. A press writes a mark record at that moment into the session file and one log line (user mark N), so the user can say when something happened. Unbound by default; set it from the Keybinds section of the overlay; -1 leaves it unbound.

keys.name: TickProbe

menu.iniOnly: measurement switch of the simulation-tick probe, no gameplay effect

keys.description: Simulation tick probe. Leases the game's own tick function once and timestamps every tick, bridge present and Reflex sleep on the thread that ran it; one log line every 10 seconds reports the tick period and body, the frame age, the wait inside the native present when the present runs inside the tick, the queue wait when it runs outside it, the slack, the Reflex sleep and the sleep-to-tick distance, the threads with the rule that paired them, and the share of presents whose frame number found its tick. Ticks and presents are numbered by the game's own frame counter, so a frame age and a wait are reported only when that counter resolved and advanced by exactly one per tick. Off = nothing is installed, nothing is read. FFXIV only.

keys.name: FlushAfterSignal

menu.iniOnly: experiment switch of the D3D11 to D3D12 hand-over, set in the ini only

keys.description: Flush the D3D11 context right after the fence Signal of the D3D11 to D3D12 hand-over, so its commands reach the driver then instead of at the game's own flush. An experiment: the cost is a driver flush and less batching, the possible gain is a shorter wait before the D3D12 side picks the frame up, and which side wins has not been measured. Off gives exactly the old hand-over.

keys.name: AdaMfgUnlock
keys.description: Optional built-in RTX 40 (Ada) multi frame generation unlock with targeted temporal correction. Memory-only, supported nvngx_dlssg.dll runtimes only, nvngx_dlssg.dll on disk is never modified. Never combine with an external unlocker. Save Settings and restart after changing.

keys.name: AutoMFG
keys.description: Experimental automatic multi frame generation multiplier for DLSS-G on RTX 40: picks 2x-4x from the real frame time and changes the count in place. Needs the Ada unlock above for anything over 2x. Never goes above 4x. Save Settings does not store the automatic choice.

keys.name: RenderPreset
keys.defaultMeans: 0 (Auto: the driver and the runtime decide)
keys.description: DLSS-G render preset for the built-in NVIDIA runtime. 0 = Auto, 1 = Preset A, 2 = Preset B, 3 = Preset C. The menu changes it while the game runs; Save Settings stores the choice.

keys.name: UIRecomposition
keys.defaultMeans: true (on while a hud-less source is in use)
keys.description: Separate UI path for DLSS-G. Only used while a hud-less image source delivers frames; read when the DLSS-G feature is created, and a change in the game recreates DLSS-G at once (frame generation restarts for a moment). The menu writes false for Off and auto for Auto and On (they act the same).

keys.name: AutoMFGMax
keys.description: Highest multiplier the automatic mode may use: 2 (2x) to 4 (4x). Values outside 2..4 count as unset.

keys.name: AutoMFGTarget
keys.defaultMeans: 0 (auto: the lower of the frame rate limit and the display refresh rate)
keys.description: Frame rate the automatic mode aims for. 0 (auto) is the lower of the frame rate limit and the display refresh rate.

keys.name: AutoMFGSelfTest
keys.description: One-off maintainer check: changes the count 2x, 3x, 4x, 3x, 2x six seconds apart and logs PASS or FAIL. Needs AutoMFG on, a fixed 3X or 4X multiplier and the INFO log level.

keys.name: AmpereMfgUnlock
keys.description: RTX 20/30 multi frame generation through a companion DLSS-G runtime in OptiScaler/dlssg_sm86. Experimental. Do not enable together with the Ada unlock. Save Settings and restart after changing.

keys.name: AmpereMfgMaxFrames
keys.description: Largest number of generated frames the companion is configured for (1 = 2X ... 5 = 6X).

keys.name: AmpereMfgKernelImage
keys.description: Interpolation kernel image written to the companion ini: Auto, PTX or Cubin.

keys.name: AmpereMfgRouter
keys.defaultMeans: Auto (picks one for the detected GPU)
keys.description: Router written to the companion ini (Auto picks one for the detected GPU).

keys.name: AmpereMfgHardwareBilinear
keys.description: Hardware bilinear sampling in the companion kernels.

keys.name: AmpereMfgOptimized
keys.description: Companion optimisation level written to its ini.

keys.name: AmpereMfgPreset
keys.description: Companion preset written to its ini.

keys.name: AmpereMfgSpoofArchToGame
keys.description: Architecture the companion reports to the game.

keys.name: AmpereMfgLogLevel
keys.description: Companion log level 0..3.

keys.name: PreviewDLSS
keys.description: Experimental isolated DLSS Super Resolution for each character preview (render size N x M, output 2N x 2M, separate histories). Needs the game's own D3D11 DLSS setup. While the DLSS pass cannot run, the spatial AA is used instead.

keys.name: JitterCorrection
keys.description: Experimental: learn the ratio between the jitter the game applies to the picture and the jitter it reports to the upscaler, and scale the reported offsets by it for every DLSS evaluate (also frame generation and the DLSS-NR path). Meant to be switched on for a test and compared with it off. Test with frame generation off first.

keys.name: PreviewAA
keys.description: Spatial anti-aliasing of the equipment preview image. Used while PreviewDLSS is off, and while the PreviewDLSS pass cannot run.

keys.name: PreviewUpscale
keys.description: PreviewAA only: the filtered image is twice the size of the original (2x preview upscaling). If the equipment preview looks zoomed or cropped, turn this off.

keys.name: PreviewGuideCapture
keys.description: Diagnostics for the DLSS path: writes guide and image dumps into OptiScaler/PreviewDLSSDiagnostics, twice per session. Leave off unless investigating.

keys.name: PreviewDebugTint
keys.description: Debug aid: mixes a colour into the preview image (magenta for spatial AA or DLSS, cyan for preview NR), so the displayed image source is visible.

keys.name: PreviewNR
keys.description: Neural Rendering for each character preview through shared images. Needs an NVIDIA card, the bridge running and nvngx_dlssnr.dll. Uses the same DlssNr settings ([DlssNr] Enabled is not needed).

keys.name: PreviewNRLingerSeconds
keys.description: Seconds a preview's NR model is kept after its window closed, so reopening the window is instant. 0 releases it at once.

keys.name: PreviewNRLate
keys.description: Show the previous frame's NR result instead of waiting for this frame's (no GPU wait, one frame of lag). Native preview image only.

keys.name: PreviewNRBeforeSR
keys.description: Experimental: run the preview's NR on the picture before the DLSS step instead of after it. Only with PreviewDLSS and PreviewNR both on.

keys.name: PreviewProbe
keys.description: Debug probe tracing how the processed preview image reaches the screen; writes images and logs to OptiScaler/PreviewDebug. Costs texture lookups per draw while on.

keys.name: PreviewDebugFlood
keys.description: Debug aid: draws the preview as solid magenta wherever the game samples it, so the replacement reach is visible.

keys.name: PreviewReplayWideShape
keys.description: Diagnostic: the signed-motion replay also takes a G-buffer draw whose camera constant buffer is a view into a larger buffer instead of exactly the 59-float4 block.

keys.name: PreviewBudget
keys.description: Limit how many preview windows get the DLSS pass and preview NR; the others keep the game's picture and are not jittered. A window is recognised by the camera constant buffer it draws with (the buffer, its first constant and the render size), without reading anything back from the GPU, so a render whose window cannot be recognised yet runs untouched. If the game's windows cannot be told apart, none of them is processed and each keeps the game's own picture; the log line `preview identity` shows it.

keys.name: PreviewMaxWindows
keys.description: How many preview windows are processed while PreviewBudget is on (1 to 8).

keys.name: JitterProbe
keys.description: Read-only look at the game's camera jitter: about every 10 seconds one log line compares applied vs reported jitter. Only reads game memory.

keys.name: JitterScaleOverride
keys.defaultMeans: 0 (off: the correction learns the ratio itself)
keys.description: Experiment: fixed scale for the reported jitter (0.25 to 1.0) instead of the learned ratio. 0 = off. Only used while JitterCorrection is on. The menu changes it live.

keys.name: JitterSource
keys.description: Experimental: fix the game's jitter at the source (full lattice, repeating cycle, told offsets). Falls back silently when unavailable. Test with frame generation off first.

keys.name: FfxivLegacyGameBuild

menu.iniOnly: persistent rollback switch of the game build handling, read once at start

keys.description: Rollback: exactly the behaviour before the address search existed. Use it to compare, or if the search misbehaves.

keys.name: FfxivUnknownBuildHooks

menu.iniOnly: persistent switch: the game-address features on a game build the table does not know

keys.description: The features that read or hook the game's code, on a game build the table has no entry for: allowed only when the search found every needed address. Has no effect on the supported build.

keys.name: FfxivForceUnknownBuild

menu.iniOnly: persistent debug switch: ignore the known-build table

keys.description: Debug: ignore the supported-build table, as if the game were patched, so the address search alone can be tried on today's executable. Leave off in normal use.

keys.name: AutomaticReShadeDepth
keys.description: Automatic scene depth for ReShade: copies the depth the upscaler is given into the back-buffer size for ReShade effects. Needs ReShade 6.8+. Switching it on takes effect within a few frames.

keys.name: DrawDiagnostics

menu.iniOnly: developer draw diagnostic: log only, writes the draw list of a few frames

keys.description: Developer switch, ini only: capture writes the draw order of a few complete frames to OptiScaler/draw-diag/<run>/ (draws.csv: one row per draw with its pixel shader CRC and stage, the reflected names of the resources and constant buffers it binds, every render target's format and size, the depth view, the viewport, blend and depth state and the tone map, first UI draw and upscale boundary markers; cb.csv: the g_LightParam position, direction and colour read back once a second). Nothing in the frame changes. The shader names are recorded when the game creates its shaders, so set it before the game starts. Any other value counts as off.

keys.name: DrawDiagnosticsFrames

menu.iniOnly: developer draw diagnostic: how many frames one capture writes

keys.description: Developer switch, ini only: how many complete frames one capture writes. Frames with fewer than 32 draws (loading screens) are skipped. 1 to 16; anything else is clamped.

keys.name: DrawDiagnosticsDelaySeconds
keys.defaultMeans: 0 (the capture starts at the first draw)

menu.iniOnly: developer draw diagnostic: how long after the game starts the capture begins

keys.description: Developer switch, ini only: seconds after the game starts before the capture begins (0 to 3600). 0 collects the opening frames; a delay puts the capture on a gameplay frame. While it waits, the constant buffers are still read once a second.

keys.name: DrawDiagnosticsKey

menu.iniOnly: developer draw diagnostic: the key that starts the capture in place of the delay

keys.description: Developer switch, ini only: a key that starts the capture instead of the delay, so it lands on the frame the player chose. A letter, a digit or F1 to F24; the key wins over the delay when both are set, and any other value means no key.

keys.name: DrawDiagnosticsDump

menu.iniOnly: developer draw diagnostic: one captured frame's targets as raw bytes for the developer check

keys.description: Developer switch, ini only: writes the render targets of one captured frame to OptiScaler/draw-diag/<run>/dump/ as raw .bin files plus facts.txt (each file's format, size, row pitch, the draw that identified it and its pointer). It takes the wetness pass target, the five G-buffer targets, the two light buffers, the hierarchical-Z target, the scene the tone map reads, the view-position buffer the water and composite draws sample, the tone map's target and the post-tone-map FP16 copy, bounded to 24 files and the byte budget in that order of importance. Nothing in the frame changes. Needs a capture of at least two frames. Up to four dumps per session, each F9 capture writing its own dump folder; mind the disk: each dump is up to the byte budget. The value ssr-pair selects a separate capture of the screen-space reflections pass instead: with DrawDiagnostics armed, it stages the pass's inputs and its output for two adjacent successful runs (raw files under OptiScaler/PreviewDebug/SsrFramePair/<run>/ with a manifest.csv; see docs/FEATURES.md). Any other value counts as off.

keys.name: DrawDiagnosticsDumpBudgetMiB

menu.iniOnly: developer draw diagnostic: the one-frame dump's byte budget, a disk and memory bound no player setting changes

keys.description: Developer switch, ini only: the byte budget of each one-frame dump (up to four dumps per session, so up to four times this on the disk), in MiB (64 to 4096; anything else is clamped). At a 3840x2160 frame's size the whole set of files is about 514 MiB with the view-position buffer (451 MiB without it) and about 546 MiB when the SSR target is written too; the default 256 holds the wetness target, the five G-buffer targets and one light buffer of such a frame (about 230 MiB). Files are taken in their order of importance, so a texture that does not fit is skipped with a line in facts.txt.

keys.name: ContactShadows
keys.description: Experimental, not verified in game, off by default. Short contact shadows before the game's sun light pass: a half-metre march along the sun direction at half the render window, multiplied into a private copy of the engine's screen-space sun mask for the one draw that samples it. Before DLSS, the tone map and the UI. The mask is recognised by its reflected name and its shape, and both measured builds are accepted: this game's light draw names it g_SamplerShadowMask and binds it as R8_UNORM, the benchmark build named it g_SamplerShadow and bound it as B8G8R8A8_UNORM; the cascade shadow atlas is refused by its format and its size. On the one benchmark frame that was dumped the term mostly did not land on contact edges, so the effect is a test, not a feature. Every screen the pass cannot measure is left exactly as it was, with one log line for the reason, and the pass stands down for the session after sixteen refused light draws in a row. The card shows the passes that ran, the light draws served and refused, and the mask of the last classified light draw.

keys.name: ContactShadowsLength
keys.description: Contact shadows (experimental, not verified in game): how far from the surface the ray looks for an occluder, in metres (0.05 to 2.0).

keys.name: ContactShadowsStrength
keys.description: Contact shadows (experimental, not verified in game): how much of the sun's visibility the contact occlusion takes away, 0 to 1. The engine's mask is 8-bit, so the term lands on whole levels of 1/255; 0 runs nothing.

keys.name: ContactShadowsSteps
keys.description: Contact shadows (experimental): steps of the march, 4 to 64, each at most one pixel long, so a thin occluder is never stepped over. More steps reach further from the surface up close, and cost more.

keys.name: ContactShadowsSunSpace
keys.defaultMeans: auto (view: the space the measurement found)

menu.iniOnly: contact shadows: which space the game reports its sun direction in, redone after a game patch

keys.description: Contact shadows (experimental, not verified in game), ini only: which space the game reports its sun direction in. auto reads as view (the direction turns with the camera while the view matrix in g_CameraParameter stays the same per scene), which is what the shipped build was measured to report; world exists for a build where that measurement has to be redone and comes out the other way round.

keys.name: ContactShadowsSunSign

menu.iniOnly: contact shadows: which way the game's sun direction points, redone after a game patch

keys.description: Contact shadows (experimental, not verified in game), ini only: which way the game's sun direction points. auto reads as toward the sun, which is what the measured vector (pointing up) reads as and what the ray has to trace; from traces the opposite way for a build whose direction turns out to be the way the light travels.

keys.name: ContactShadowsDump

menu.iniOnly: contact shadows: writes one frame's mask, term, depth and camera bytes for the developer check

keys.description: Contact shadows (experimental, not verified in game), ini only: writes one frame out for the developer check, at the first sun light draw that runs this many seconds after the game starts. The frame holds the engine's sun mask before the pass (under a file name that says its format: mask-before.r8 for this build's R8_UNORM mask, one byte per texel), the half-resolution term, the mask copy the draw sampled, the depth, the camera matrices and the sun vector, plus a text file with the sizes and the keys; all of them from the same GPU frame, so a comparison has none of the run-to-run noise two runs have. The same key also keeps the bytecode of every shader that declares the sun mask from the moment the game creates it (the light shader is created while the game loads, so no capture of its draw holds it), and the dump writes those blobs beside the mask: the mask's texels and the channel the light draw reads are what settle which level of the mask means sunlight. Files go to the contact-dump folder beside the DLL. 0 writes nothing.

keys.name: ShadowMapping
keys.defaultMeans: false (today's behaviour, the engine's own deferred light)
keys.description: Experimental, not yet verified in game, off by default. Two levers at the game's own deferred light, both at their idle by default: the screen-space sun/shadow mask the light draw squares gets a lifted shadowed floor at the light draws (the lift applies to the value the square shares, so the key reads linearly in the picture, and 0 is the engine's own mask byte for byte), and the deferred composite's ambient probe table gets a night lift - the header's global sky-SH scale (the term the shipped ambient knob never moves) and the per-probe SH reciprocal scale, scaled in ONE patch dispatch on the composite draw so it composes with the shipped ambient knob's scale. Both levers key on the frame's own light colour: full effect at night, nothing in day, a blend across the two provisional thresholds awaiting the capture. The mask lift shares one copy per frame with the contact shadows pass when that feature is armed and runs its own copy at the light draws when it is not. Every state the module cannot measure is left exactly as it was, with one log line for the reason, and sixty-four refused light draws in a row stand the mask route down for the session with one line.

keys.name: ShadowLift
keys.defaultMeans: 0.0 (the engine's own mask byte for byte, and nothing runs)
keys.description: Shadow mapping: the shadow floor of the sun/shadow mask's copy at the light draws, as the share of the mask's unlit depth the light term gives back. The engine's own shader squares the mask, so the remap is applied to the value the square shares (m'^2 = m^2 + (1-m^2)*Lift) and the copy carries its square root: the key then reads linearly in the picture. The day/night curve scales it.

keys.name: ShadowEdgeSoftness
keys.description: Shadow mapping: how far the lifted mask's edges feather, 0-2 mask pixels as the tent's reach over the lifted copy (a reach of at most one pixel reads the 3x3 kernel, two the 5x5 one). It feathers the lift: a lift of 0 stays the byte-exact passthrough whatever this says.

keys.name: NightAmbientLift
keys.defaultMeans: 1.0 (the engine's own ambient table, and nothing runs)
keys.description: Shadow mapping: the night multiplier on the composite's ambient probe table - the header's global sky-SH scale (the table's byte 4, the night's dominant term the shipped ambient knob never touches) and the 64 probes' SH reciprocal scale (the field at byte 112+192k, the engine's own SkyRecip entry shape). One dispatch, appended after the shipped knob's entries so the multipliers compose. 1.0 is the engine's own picture, above 1.0 brightens the night's fill, below 1.0 (down to 0.25) darkens it; the day/night curve applies it too.

keys.name: NightCurveToggle
keys.description: Shadow mapping, ini only: the day/night curve both levers key on. Its input is the visible sun's elevation as the fog post states it (the fog sun's world y): no lift while the sun is above 1 degree below the horizon, full by 7 degrees below it, a smoothstep between (0 on a daylight frame, about 0.34 at 3 degrees below, about 0.96 at 6). It asks for the fog post's sun row whatever the god rays key says; when no fog sun has landed in the last 120 rendered frames the curve falls back to the main view's g_LightParam colour (full effect at night, zero in day, between 0.15 and 0.9 Rec.709 luminance). off pins the full effect at all hours: the debugging switch that makes a noon A/B possible.

keys.name: CharaAmbient
keys.description: Lighting tab (experimental, not verified in game): the character draws' own ambient block (g_AmbientParam, the 160-byte table the chara shaders declare beside the composite's probe array; a character draw is a shader that also declares g_CustomizeParameter, the world's materials are left alone). The lift scales that block's reciprocal scale - the scalar every ambient term a character's shader reads is multiplied with - for exactly those draws, so characters read their own local fill at night and the engine's own block in day. The lift keys on the frame's own light colour (the same day/night curve the shadow mapping card keys on, read no-wait from the sun's light draw; the curve's two luminance thresholds are provisional until the five-stop capture runs). The block's colour bytes and every field beside the scalar keep their bits. No game resource is ever written; an unmeasurable state is left exactly as it was, with one log line for the reason; and the module stands down for the session after sixty-four of its own draws in a row are left alone.

keys.name: CharaAmbientLift
keys.defaultMeans: 1.0 (the engine's own block, and nothing runs)
keys.description: Lighting tab: the night multiplier on the chara ambient block's reciprocal scale, 0.5 to 2.0. 1.0 is the engine's own picture and runs nothing at all; below 1.0 dims the characters' own ambient fill, above 1.0 lifts it. The block's colour bytes and every field beside the scalar keep their bits. The day/night curve applies this key too.

keys.name: EnginePassOverrides
keys.description: Experimental, not verified in game, off by default. Lets this fork change one of the engine's own rendering parameters for a single draw without touching the game's memory: the draw is recognised by the parameter buffers its shader declares, the buffer is copied on the GPU, scaled or set, bound for that one draw and the game's own buffer put back. Every screen the module cannot measure is left exactly as it was, with one log line for the reason, and it stands down for the session after sixty-four of one knob's draws in a row are refused.

keys.name: AmbientSkyVisibilityScale
keys.description: Engine pass overrides (experimental, not verified in game): scales the sky light the ambient probes contribute, 0 to 2: the probe's sky visibility where the composite honours it, and the probe's SH reciprocal scale everywhere, which also dims the probe's share of the indirect specular reflection. 1.0 is the engine's own picture and runs nothing at all; lower values darken the flat sky-lit fill of a night without touching the baked probe values, the direct light or the shadows.

keys.name: WetnessOverride
keys.description: Engine pass overrides (experimental, not verified in game): the wetness the engine applies to the ground. -1 is the engine's own value and runs nothing; 0.0 forces dry ground and 1.0 full wetness, whatever the weather is, and the engine's own dryness blend follows the forced value. The engine's rain-exposure mask still decides where the ground is sheltered, so the gloss appears under open sky and not under cover.

keys.name: AmbientOcclusion
keys.description: Ambient occlusion (experimental; tried in game in one session on 2026-11-01, where the user confirmed the pass works, and the fixed picture and the pause have not been judged again). This fork computes its own ambient occlusion from the game's depth and its G-buffer normal, once a frame, into a texture of the engine's own size and format, and every draw of that frame from the reader that completes the pass's three inputs onward that would sample the engine's screen-space occlusion samples this fork's for that one call; a reader of that frame before the completing one keeps the engine's texture, and the game's own texture is bound again afterwards. Nothing of the game is written and no shader of the game is replaced. Any frame the pass cannot measure keeps the engine's texture; after sixty-four frames in a row left alone (one count a frame, at its first wait or its refusal) the module pauses, inspects every reader of one frame again about 2.7 seconds later (120 frames at 45 frames a second) and re-arms at the first frame it can serve. Strength or blend at 0 runs nothing at all.

keys.name: AmbientOcclusionRadius
keys.description: Ambient occlusion: how far around a pixel the search looks, in metres of world. A larger radius darkens more of a room and costs nothing extra on the GPU; only the picture changes. 1.0 m is a doorway's worth.

keys.name: AmbientOcclusionStrength
keys.description: Ambient occlusion: how much of the computed occlusion is applied. 1.0 is the algorithm's own answer, above 1 exaggerates it, and 0.0 runs nothing at all: the engine's own texture stays bound.

keys.name: AmbientOcclusionBlend
keys.defaultMeans: 0.5 (half of this fork's darkening on top of the engine's own)
keys.description: Ambient occlusion: how much of this fork's occlusion is applied on top of the engine's own. The two are multiplied, so 1.0 applies both, 0.5 applies half of this fork's contribution, and 0.0 runs nothing: the engine's own texture stays bound. A term this fork finds nothing in leaves the engine's occlusion exactly as it was. Lower it first if the picture looks too dark overall.

keys.name: AmbientOcclusionQuality
keys.description: Ambient occlusion: how many depth taps a direction the search takes - 4, 8 or 16. The one setting that changes what the pass costs on the GPU, roughly in proportion. Anything but low, medium or high reads as medium.

keys.name: Puddles
keys.description: Puddles (experimental, not verified in game). Rain makes the ground glossy; this fork adds the standing water, in two stages that read one noise field anchored to the world. Once a frame, before the light passes, it copies one of the engine's own G-buffer targets and replaces the gloss channel of the ground where a puddle is, binding that copy for every draw of the frame that binds the same target object as the frame's first reader. At the tone-map draw it then darkens the pool's lit colour and adds a marched reflection of the scene to it, with water's Fresnel: the mirror is the picture the frame has already drawn, not the engine's 256-square environment probe. The engine's own wetness amount ramps both stages up with the rain and down as it dries (while the engine pass's wetness knob is armed, the amount it forces is the one the engine's own draws read, so it is the one the puddles use too), so there is no timer here and nothing is remembered between frames. Nothing of the game is written and no shader of the game is replaced; a frame the pass cannot serve is skipped with one log line, and only a frame it cannot do the work for (an allocation, a draw, a throw, a target of a format it cannot copy) counts towards the sixty-four in a row that switch it off for the session. A coverage of 0 is today's picture.

keys.name: PuddlesCoverage
keys.defaultMeans: 0.42 (about a third of the up-facing ground at full rain, measured over the field's own 64-cell period)
keys.description: Puddles: how much of the ground that faces up becomes puddle at full rain. 0.42 puts about a third of it in pools (measured on the shader's own field over one full 64-cell period): the rest stays damp with the engine's own glossy sheen, which is what makes the pools read as pools. 0.0 runs nothing at all.

keys.name: PuddlesScale
keys.defaultMeans: 6.0 metres (the median pool 4.3 m across, the largest tenth 11.5 m, measured on a 60 m patch)
keys.description: Puddles: the size of one patch of the noise field, in metres: a pool is a few cells across, so 6.0 puts the median pool at about four metres across and the largest tenth near twelve, which is what a 60 m patch of the field measured. Larger values make broad sheets, smaller ones a wet grain. The field is anchored to the world, so it stays where it is while the camera moves.

keys.name: PuddlesSoftness
keys.defaultMeans: 0.03 (a 0.8 m edge at the default scale)
keys.description: Puddles: the half-width of a puddle's edge, in noise units. 0.03 gives the sub-metre edge the reference's stone has (0.8 m at the default scale); near 0.0 the puddles get a hard outline, which also shows the 8 bits the engine's target is stored in.

keys.name: PuddlesGlossTarget
keys.description: Puddles: which of the engine's G-buffer targets carries the channel to shape. 1 is the material pack, whose alpha is the gloss the engine's composite reads. Only the engine's 8-bit targets can be shaped: 3 is a 16-bit target and 4 is the world-space normal this pass reads to decide what faces up, so neither is offered (an ini value of either binds the engine's own target unchanged and says so in the log). The pools are kept off ground the engine renders dry, read from the engine's gloss in G-buffer 1: with target 2 there is no engine gloss to read, so both stages draw no pool (one log line says so).

keys.name: PuddlesGlossChannel
keys.description: Puddles: which channel of that target is replaced - r, g, b or a, anything else reads as a. The alpha of the material pack is the gloss. The other three channels are the engine's own bits, untouched, so a channel whose meaning has not been measured cannot be corrupted by this pass. The red channel of target 1 is the one pair the pass refuses: the engine reads that byte as a selector and chooses the surface encoding by it, so writing it tints the ground, and the pass then binds the engine's own target and says so in the log.

keys.name: PuddlesGlossWet
keys.defaultMeans: 1.0 (wetter than the engine's own wet ground, whose gloss sits at about 0.83)
keys.description: Puddles: the channel value of a mirror-wet surface. The engine's own gloss sits at about 0.83 on wet ground, so 1.0 is wetter than the weather; 0.0 is for a channel that is a roughness instead of a gloss. Whichever way round it is, the puddles take this value and the dry ground keeps the engine's own. Inside the pool this value is also what a mirrored ray that found nothing falls back to: the engine's own probe reflection of that ground, sharpened, then darkened by PuddlesDarkening - never black.

keys.name: PuddlesReflection
keys.description: Puddles: the mirrored reflection of the scene at the tone-map draw. true marches the frame's own view positions from each pool texel and adds what the ray hits with water's Fresnel (about 2 % straight on, most of it at a grazing angle). Judge it from the reference's own pose: level, at eye height, the fountain six to ten metres ahead - below about three metres the Fresnel makes the mirror invisible and the darkening carries the pool. false is the darkening alone, which is the A/B a session needs to judge the shape before the mirror. Nothing is remembered between frames, so the pass cannot ghost on its own; it is one sample of the scene per texel, so an upscaler or frame generation may shimmer or smear the hit's edge, and that is expected rather than a fault.

keys.name: PuddlesReflectionStrength
keys.description: Puddles: how much of the Fresnel reflection the marched colour is added with. 0.0 is the darkening alone; 1.0 is the scene's own colour at full Fresnel, which is a perfect mirror where the angle is right.

keys.name: PuddlesDarkening
keys.defaultMeans: 0.45 (a pool keeps a little over half of the lit colour)
keys.description: Puddles: how much of the lit colour a full puddle takes away. This is the part that makes the ground read as water instead of varnish, and the reference's wet stone is dark even where no reflection lands; 0.45 keeps a little over half of the colour inside a pool. It is also the risky half of the look at night: a night stone sits near 0.10, so a full pool at 0.45 lands near 0.05 and reads as a hole where the mirror misses. 0.0 with the reflection off is the stage's identity, so nothing is copied and nothing is drawn.

keys.name: PuddlesRipple
keys.description: Puddles: how much a fixed ripple field tilts the mirror's normal. The slope comes from the same world-anchored noise as the pool, so it is the same in every frame and cannot crawl; 0.0 is a flat mirror of the stone joints.

keys.name: PuddlesReflectionSteps
keys.description: Puddles: how many taps the mirrored reflection's march takes. This is the one setting that changes what the tone-map stage costs on the GPU, roughly in proportion; a pool's mirror is a wide, smooth thing, so the default is half of the water reflection's 48. The cost is expected to be 0.4 to 1.3 ms at 1080p, unmeasured on a real card: about 690,000 pool texels (a third of a 1920x1080 window) times 24 taps, plus the window's ring. A session reads the pass's own figure from the log line instead of trusting the estimate.

keys.name: PuddlesReach
keys.description: Puddles: how far from the camera a pool may sit, in metres. The G-buffer beneath a forward draw - the ocean, the lakes, the rivers - is the up-facing ground under the water, so past the reach the tone-map stage keeps the engine's own texel instead of painting pools onto the water. The measured water blotches sat between 25 and 40 m with the camera at eye height; the beach pools a player reads sit inside 24 m. 0 disables the gate.

keys.name: LightShafts
keys.description: Light shafts (experimental, not verified in game), off by default. The sun's light is scattered through the frame: the depth buffer gives the sky, a radial blur carries it toward the sun's position on screen, and the result is added to a copy of the lit scene that the tone map reads for that one draw. The game's own scene is only read, never written, and every frame the module cannot measure is left exactly as it was, with one log line for the reason; it stands down for the session after sixty-four of its own draws in a row are left alone. It is inactive while the engine's scene HDR is on, because that path replaces the tone map this pass draws before. Judge it with the sun low in the frame, behind trees or a roof edge.

keys.name: LightShaftsIntensity
keys.description: Light shafts (experimental): how much light the shafts add, 0 to 2, as a share of the white the pass reads (the tone map's own exposure multiplier's reciprocal, held between 0.15 and the measured 0.838). 0.00 turns the pass off and the frame costs one test per draw and nothing else; 1.0 is a clear glow around a low sun (about a tenth of that white); 2.00 is the strongest the slider goes - the addition is bounded by each pixel's room to that white, so no key pushes a channel past the white the pass reads. A wrong-high live exposure on a much darker frame still over-lights it, and while the exposure has not landed the white is the band's dark end, 0.15.

keys.name: LightShaftsDecay
keys.description: Light shafts (experimental): how fast a sample toward the sun fades, 0.80 to 1.00. Higher keeps the shafts reaching across the frame; lower keeps them a glow around the sun's own pixels.

keys.name: LightShaftsSamples
keys.description: Light shafts (experimental): the blur's sample count, 16 to 96. More samples are smoother and cost more on the GPU; the pass runs at half the render size.

keys.name: LightShaftsDensity
keys.description: Light shafts (experimental): how far each sample reaches toward the sun, 0.10 to 1.50. Above 1.00 the blur samples past the sun, which spreads the shafts over the whole frame.

keys.name: LightShaftsColor
keys.description: Light shafts (experimental): which colour the shafts take. auto is the sun's own colour - the engine's colour for that light when it reports one, and otherwise the sky's colour around the sun's screen position (only sky pixels are sampled, so what stands in front of the sun cannot tint the shafts), which is what today's build needs because its directional light reports a zero colour; a frame with no sky around the sun, or one whose sky is below a small brightness floor, adds nothing at all and is not counted as a refusal. white is a neutral shaft tinted only by the intensity key, for telling a colour problem from a geometry problem; it has no floor of its own, so a white run at night glows.

keys.name: GodraysVolumetric
keys.description: God rays: the volumetric march (experimental, not verified in game). A per-pixel ray march through the air in front of each pixel, at a quarter of the render size: each sample's shadow is read from the game's own cascade shadow atlas (all four cascades, the same map the ground shadows are built from), the medium from the game's own live fog state, scattered around the shadow light and summed with extinction, and the result is added to a copy of the lit scene (the sky included, up to its own 99th percentile) that the tone map reads for that one draw - bounded by the frame's own white, like the radial light shafts beside it, and the last stage of the same tone-map chain. The beams follow the shadow light, which can sit above the visible sun, and there are none when that light is behind or beside the camera or dim. The game's own scene is only read, never written, and every frame the march cannot measure is left exactly as the chain left it, with one log line for the reason; it stands down for the session after sixty-four refused draws in a row. Inactive while the engine's scene HDR is on, because that path replaces the tone map this march draws before. As a standalone effect it has reached its limit: with no engine fog (clear weather binds a height profile with every density zero) its medium is zero and there is nothing to scatter in, and where the engine does fog it showed nothing in play (74 frames with beams, none visible, 2026-11-07), so it stays off by default.

keys.name: GodraysSteps
keys.description: God rays: the march's sample count, 16 to 96. More samples are smoother and cost more on the GPU; the march runs at a quarter of the render size by default.

keys.name: GodraysResolution
keys.description: God rays: the march's own resolution. quarter is the default and the cheap one; half doubles the taps for a softer term.

keys.name: GodraysFogBoost
keys.description: God rays: a multiplier on the density the game's own fog profile gives, 0 to 2, on top of GodraysDensity. 1.0 keeps the engine's own profile (its shape, its fall-off with height); the march thickens or thins the air the game is already fogging.

keys.name: GodraysHeightLift
keys.description: God rays: a multiplier on the height falloff of the game's own fog profile, 0 to 2. 1.0 is the engine's own shape; 0.0 flattens it to a uniform haze; 2.0 doubles the height gradient.

keys.name: GodraysIntensity
keys.description: God rays: how much light the march adds, 0 to 2, as a share of the white the pass reads (the tone map's own exposure multiplier's reciprocal, held between 0.15 and the measured 0.838). 0.00 turns the march off and the frame costs one test per draw and nothing else; each pixel's room to that white bounds the addition, so no key pushes a channel past the white the pass reads.

keys.name: GodraysColor
keys.description: God rays: which colour the beams take. auto is the sun's own colour - the engine's colour for that light when it reports one, and otherwise the sky's colour around the sun's screen position (only sky pixels are sampled, so what stands in front of the sun cannot tint the beams). white is a neutral beam tinted only by the intensity key, for telling a colour problem from a geometry problem. enginefog is the game's own fog colour rule: the colour it fogs that very pixel with, built from its own sky texture and weight LUT - the beams then take exactly the tint the game's own fog post applies beside them.

keys.name: GodraysShadowSoftness
keys.description: God rays: the shadow compare's taps, 0 to 2. 0 is a point compare (the cheapest), 1 samples two texels at a cascade's boundary and 2 samples four. A cascade's atlas texel spans a world footprint the march reads per sample, and this is the knob that softens the banding that footprint can show - at the cost of the same multiple in atlas reads.

keys.name: GodraysJitter
keys.description: God rays: the per-pixel offset of the march's samples (the radial shafts' own hash, a function of the pixel alone). false makes a still scene perfectly still and shows the march's own lattice; true trades a little noise for smoother beams, which the upscaler's temporal accumulation then cleans.

keys.name: GodraysPhaseBoost
keys.description: God rays: narrows or widens the glow around the shadow light, 0 to 2. 1.0 is neutral (GodraysAnisotropy as it is); higher concentrates the beams toward the light (the lobe's narrowness is divided by this), lower spreads them; 0.0 is an even glow in every direction.

keys.name: GodraysDensity
keys.description: God rays: how dense the air is for the beams, 0 to 200, in units of 0.001 per metre at the camera's own height (20 is 0.02 per metre). The game's own fog is about 0.001 per metre there, far too thin to show a beam, so this is an artistic constant: higher makes the beams stronger and darkens the air behind them (extinction). The fog's shape (height, fall-off) is still the game's own.

keys.name: GodraysAnisotropy
keys.description: God rays: how narrow the glow around the shadow light is, 0 to 0.95 (the Henyey-Greenstein g). 0.0 spreads the light evenly in every direction; 0.8 keeps it within about 25 degrees of the light.

keys.name: Gi
keys.description: Screen-space light bounce (experimental, not verified in game). The tone-map chain's own bounce stage after the volumetric march: at a half of the render size, K cosine-distributed rays leave every pixel's G-buffer normal, each ray is marched against the game's own view positions up to the range key with thickness rejection, and a hit sends back its own linear scene value - the scene's stored texel squared (the engine stores the square root of its composed sum), with the surface's own colour left in, so a warm floor sends warm light and a lamp its own light. Rays that find no hit add zero. The estimate is smoothed once by a dense 5x5 stencil that averages every pixel the pass traced (a pixel whose rays all missed is a valid zero) and skips only the ones it could not trace, and is added to a copy of the lit scene through the same white-bounded addition the other added-light stages carry: no key pushes a channel past the white the pass reads. The origin pixel's own albedo multiplier is the albedo carrier's stored value squared (the G-buffer target the engine's own composite squares on read), with the material pack's diffuse weight, and the engine's own special material rows are answered with nothing. The sky keeps its own value; every frame the stage cannot measure is left exactly as the chain left it, with one log line for the reason; it stands down for the session after sixty-four counted declines in a row; it is inactive while the engine's scene HDR is on, because that path replaces the tone map this stage draws before.

keys.name: GiRays
keys.description: Screen-space light bounce: the rays one pixel casts, 1 to 8. More rays fill the hemisphere the corner sees and cost more.

keys.name: GiSteps
keys.description: Screen-space light bounce: the march's steps, 8 to 32. More steps confirm a nearer crossing; the cost is one read per step and per ray.

keys.name: GiRange
keys.description: Screen-space light bounce: how far from the pixel a ray reaches, in metres of world, 1 to 20. Rays past the range carry nothing; small radii keep the bounce local (tight corners, no ghosting across the scene).

keys.name: GiStrength
keys.description: Screen-space light bounce: how much of the bounce the pass adds, 0 to 1. 0.00 turns the stage off (the frame costs one test per draw, nothing else); 1.00 is the full diffuse bounce (a surface under a uniform environment reflects it whole), and the default 0.55 is the calibrated amount: a lamp-lit wall bleeds visibly onto its neighbours while a flat open area stays under 1 %. Each pixel's room to the white the pass reads bounds the addition, so no key pushes a channel past that white.

keys.name: GiResolution
keys.description: Screen-space light bounce: the pass's own resolution. half is the default; quarter halves the march's cost.

keys.name: DepthOfField
keys.description: Depth of field (experimental, not verified in game). This fork's own DoF at the tone-map chain's last stage: the scene is packed with an analytic circle of confusion (computed from the camera's own depth against the focus distance, the game's own Weight2 + CoC-LUT pair's pack shape), blurred on a disc at a quarter of the render window split near and far (the game's own DownScale4x4 + DiscBlurNear shapes), and merged back before the engine's own tone map reads the picture - the order the game's own DoF family runs in on the benchmark. The game's own scene is only read, never written, and every frame the stage cannot measure is left exactly as the chain left it, with one log line for the reason; it stands down for the session after sixty-four refused draws in a row. Inactive while the engine's scene HDR is on, because that path replaces the tone map this stage draws before.

keys.name: DofMode
keys.description: Depth of field, the look. distance is the gameplay look and the default: nothing nearer than the start distance (the larger of twice the focus distance and 20 m) is touched, the far background softens beyond it (a thin-lens curve that reaches its full softness at eight times the start, a blur radius capped at 0.75 % of the window height and a mix capped at 25 % of the blurred picture), the near side never blurs, and the auto focus follows the centre of the screen smoothly. cinematic is the first release's look, kept as it was: a sharp band around the focus plane and a strong blur of everything behind it at every angle (reach DofAperture). When the game's own depth of field draws in a frame, the stage leaves that frame to it in both looks.

keys.name: DofFocusMode
keys.description: Depth of field: what the focus plane is. auto follows the depth the camera looks at (the render window's centre pixel, reconstructed through the game's own camera - the classic follow-focus behaviour; the distance look smooths it over time and ignores the sky); manual pins the plane to DofFocusDistance.

keys.name: DofFocusDistance
keys.description: Depth of field, manual focus only: the focus plane's distance from the camera, in metres (the metres the game's own fog profile reads). 0.5 to 500.

keys.name: DofAperture
keys.description: Depth of field, cinematic look only: how far the blur reaches, as a fraction of the window's height - the same number reads as the same circle at 1440p and at 1080p. 0.050 spans 72 pixels of a 1440p render at the deepest defocus; 0 turns the cinematic look off (the frame costs one test per draw). The distance look has its own fixed radius and ignores this key. 0.005 to 0.12.

keys.name: DofStrength
keys.description: Depth of field: how much of the blur the merge mixes in, 0 to 1. 0 is off (the frame costs one test per draw, nothing else); the default 0.80 is a visible softness without hazing the whole frame. In the distance look the mix is this key times 0.25, so 1.00 mixes 25 % of the blurred picture at the far limit.

keys.name: DofSteps
keys.description: Depth of field: the disc's taps, 16 to 48. More taps are a smoother disc's edge and cost more on the GPU at a quarter of the render size; 24 is the default disc.

keys.name: Atmosphere
keys.defaultMeans: true (on by default; false is today's picture)
keys.description: Atmosphere (experimental; on by default).
