Aerial perspective with height and a sun lobe, the tone-map chain's stage between the light bounce and depth of field: distant surfaces sink into the air in front of them (out = scene x T + inscatter x (1 - T), T = exp(-tau), tau the optical depth of an exponential height medium along the view ray from a start distance to the surface; the inscatter is the engine's own fog colour pulled toward a neutral grey of its own brightness plus a Henyey-Greenstein lobe centred on the sun disc the sky draws). Sky pixels and everything nearer than the start distance are left exactly as they are, and the engine's own fog density at the camera scales this one down so foggy weather is not fogged twice. It runs after the engine's luminance measure, so eye adaptation does not undo it. The game's own scene is only read, never written, and every frame the stage cannot measure is left exactly as the chain left it, with one log line for the reason; it stands down for the session after sixty-four refused draws in a row. Inactive while the engine's scene HDR is on, because that path replaces the tone map this stage draws before.

keys.name: AtmosphereDensity
keys.description: Atmosphere: how thick the air is at the camera's own height, per kilometre. 0 is off (the frame costs one test per draw, nothing else). At the default 1.5 per km (with the 50 m start) a surface 200 m away keeps about 80 % of its own light, one 500 m away about 51 %.

keys.name: AtmosphereHeightFalloff
keys.description: Atmosphere: how fast the air thins with height above the camera, per metre (0.01 is a scale height of 100 m). 0 is a homogeneous haze.

keys.name: AtmosphereStart
keys.description: Atmosphere: nothing nearer than this is fogged, in metres, so the first metres around the character stay clear whatever the density is.

keys.name: AtmospherePhaseG
keys.description: Atmosphere: the sun lobe's anisotropy (Henyey-Greenstein g). 0 spreads the sun's light over the whole sky; 0.7 is a glow that falls to a tenth at about 30 degrees from the sun; 0.95 a tight one. Forward scattering only.

keys.name: AtmosphereSunStrength
keys.description: Atmosphere: how much of the frame's white the sun's glow adds at the sun, where the air is thick. 0 takes the glow away.

keys.name: AtmosphereSkyStrength
keys.description: Atmosphere: the ambient light of the air as a multiple of the engine's own fog colour (which matches the horizon sky). 1 fades distant surfaces to it.

keys.name: AtmosphereNightDensity
keys.description: Atmosphere: the share of the density that stays when the light is the moon's (the light draw's own luminance decides how much of the day is left). 1 keeps all of it, 0 takes the haze away at night.

keys.name: AtmosphereNeutral
keys.description: Atmosphere: how much of the haze's colour is replaced by a grey of the same brightness. 0 keeps the engine's own fog colour (the cyan of a clear sky), 1 is a pure neutral; the reference look's far haze is a bright near-neutral white. It does not depend on the sun and needs none.

keys.name: EngineLight
keys.description: Engine light controls (experimental): changes the light the ENGINE computes at night, at the source - the moon, the ambient, the water's own copies of both and the point lights (lamps) - weighted by the shared night curve, with the engine's exposure held so its eye adaptation does not undo the change. A daylight frame is the engine's own picture byte for byte. The controls wait a few seconds at the start of the night for the engine's exposure to settle on its own light, latch it, then fade in over a second. While this master is on the composite ambient belongs to this module and Shadow mapping's Night ambient lift yields (no double application). It asks Shadow mapping to keep the light-colour feed running whatever Shadow lift and Night ambient lift say; it is inactive while the engine's scene HDR is on. It replaces the retired Night grade (NightGrade, NightDarkness, NightKnee, NightTint).

keys.name: EngineLightReferenceAB
keys.description: Engine light: the live A/B. True shows the engine's own light for as long as it is set (every factor 1, no exposure compensation); the exposure latch keeps following the engine meanwhile, so clearing it puts the look back on a fresh latch. The card's "Show the engine's own light (A/B)" box sets it.

keys.name: EngineLightMoon
keys.description: Engine light: the moon's colour multiplier at night (the directional light's diffuse and specular colour). 1 is the engine's own; the default 0.1 is the measured distance to the reference look (low-to-medium confidence). On the water pass the Water moon key replaces this one.

keys.name: EngineLightMoonTintR
keys.description: Engine light: per-channel multiplier on the moon colour, red. 1 is neutral.

keys.name: EngineLightMoonTintG
keys.description: Engine light: per-channel multiplier on the moon colour, green. 1 is neutral.

keys.name: EngineLightMoonTintB
keys.description: Engine light: per-channel multiplier on the moon colour, blue. 1 is neutral.

keys.name: EngineLightAmbient
keys.description: Engine light: the ambient (the spherical-harmonics probe table) multiplier. 1 is the engine's own. While Engine light is on this module owns the composite ambient and Shadow mapping's Night ambient lift yields.

keys.name: EngineLightAmbientTintR
keys.description: Engine light: per-channel multiplier on the ambient, red. 1 is neutral.

keys.name: EngineLightAmbientTintG
keys.description: Engine light: per-channel multiplier on the ambient, green. 1 is neutral.

keys.name: EngineLightAmbientTintB
keys.description: Engine light: per-channel multiplier on the ambient, blue. 1 is neutral.

keys.name: EngineLightWaterMoon
keys.description: Engine light: the water pass's own moon term. It REPLACES the Moon key on the water pass - they do not stack: at 1 the water keeps the engine's moon whatever Moon says.

keys.name: EngineLightWaterAmbient
keys.description: Engine light: the water's own ambient block multiplier. 1 is the engine's own.

keys.name: EngineLightWaterTintR
keys.description: Engine light: per-channel multiplier on the water's ambient block, red (toward neutral at 1).

keys.name: EngineLightWaterTintG
keys.description: Engine light: per-channel multiplier on the water's ambient block, green (toward neutral at 1).

keys.name: EngineLightWaterTintB
keys.description: Engine light: per-channel multiplier on the water's ambient block, blue (toward neutral at 1).

keys.name: EngineLightLamps
keys.description: Engine light: the point lights' contribution multiplier (every lamp volume of both light passes), applied through the blend factor of the lamp draws, so it needs no knowledge of their constants. 1 is the engine's own and touches nothing.

keys.name: EngineLightExposure
keys.description: Engine light: the exposure mode. 0 = off (the engine adapts freely and takes back part of the darkening), 1 = auto hold (the picture keeps the exposure the engine had on its own light, latched after it settled and rescaled at the tone map by s_hold / s_now), 2 = manual factor (EngineLightExposureManual).

keys.name: EngineLightExposureManual
keys.description: Engine light: the manual compensation factor of exposure mode 2, a multiplier on the scene eased in with the night weight.

keys.name: EngineLightForceNightWeight

menu.iniOnly: benchmark pin: the night weight is 1 whatever the night curve says

keys.description: Engine light: pins the night weight to 1 whatever the night curve says (the benchmark never reads a light, so its cost is measured at a fixed weight). The exposure hold skips its settle wait and bootstraps from the first reading. Leave it false in play.

keys.name: FlareCard
keys.description: Lens flare (experimental, not verified in game). The engine's own flare family with each part's amount in your hands: the ring's colour, the sun sprite's colour (the ghost orbs follow what the game copies from their sprite), the step the copies march by, and the veil's skip. Recognition is by the reflected name of each draw of the family, never a bytecode fingerprint; a frame the card cannot address is left as the engine's own drawing of it, with one log line saying so, and it stands down for the session after sixty-four of its own draws are left alone in a row. Every default is today's picture; the master switch is off, so a fresh ini is the game's own flare.

keys.name: FlareParts
keys.description: Lens flare: which parts of the family are in the picture, as the bits ring 1, sun+orbs 2, veil 4. A clear bit removes that part: the ring's or the sun's colour goes to 0 through its own patch (never a skip, its buffers belong to the scene the HDR composite reads), and the veil's add is skipped for its draw alone (its colour and bias ride its own four vertices' data, so no patch can reach it).

keys.name: FlareRingScale
keys.description: Lens flare: the ring's colour, 0 to 2. 1.0 is the engine's own picture; 0.0 removes the ring and nothing else - the sun, the ghosts and the veil keep the values they were at.

keys.name: FlareSunScale
keys.description: Lens flare: the sun sprite's colour, 0 to 2. The three radial blurs copy the sprite, so the ghost orbs and the veil's 1x1 input empty out with it: 0.0 removes the whole of it and leaves the game's own bloom where it was - the glare chain's weight is the bloom's own, not the flare's.

keys.name: FlareGhostScale
keys.description: Lens flare: the step the ghost copies march by, 0 to 2. 0.0 collapses the three radial-blur passes into one disc - the ghosts merge into the sprite, which sits untouched at its own value - and 2.0 spreads them twice as far.

keys.name: ScreenSpaceReflections
keys.description: Screen-space reflections (experimental, not verified in game). This fork computes its own reflection for the water surfaces: once a frame, before the first water draw, it marches the game's view-position buffer against the scene the frame has already rendered, into a texture of the engine's planar reflection map's own size and format, and every water draw of that frame that would sample the engine's map samples this fork's for that one call; the game's own texture is bound again afterwards. Where the march finds nothing the engine's own texel is kept untouched, no shader of the game is replaced, and the module switches itself off for the session after sixty-four refused water draws in a row. A blend of 0 runs nothing at all.

keys.name: ScreenSpaceReflectionsSteps
keys.description: Screen-space reflections: how many taps the ray march takes. The one setting that changes what the pass costs on the GPU, roughly in proportion. More steps find thinner and farther reflections, not brighter ones.

keys.name: ScreenSpaceReflectionsThickness
keys.description: Screen-space reflections: how deep behind a crossing ray a surface still counts as the one the ray hit, in metres of world. Too small and a thin reflection (a railing, a mast) is missed; too large and a wall the ray passed a metre ago paints the water.

keys.name: ScreenSpaceReflectionsBlend
keys.defaultMeans: 0.5 (this fork's reflection where the march finds one, mixed with the engine's own map)
keys.description: Screen-space reflections: how much of this fork's reflection replaces the engine's own where the march found something. 1.0 is this one only, 0.5 mixes the two equally, and 0.0 runs nothing: the engine's own map stays bound. The default mixes them, because a 100 % traced reflection over a shallow shore reads as a hard cut-out instead of water.

keys.name: ScreenSpaceReflectionsFade
keys.defaultMeans: 0.15 (15% of the picture at its edges)
keys.description: Screen-space reflections: the fraction of the picture at its edges over which a reflection is trusted less and less, so a hit that runs out of screen fades out instead of ending at a hard line. 0.0 trusts a hit right up to the edge.

keys.name: ScreenSpaceReflectionsDiagnostic

menu.iniOnly: developer SSR diagnostic: F7 cycles test modes of the screen-space reflections pass

keys.description: Developer switch, ini only: turns on the screen-space reflections pass's live diagnostic. While it is on, F7 cycles sixteen test modes (A to P) that change how the pass binds, draws, times and restores its work (A is the pass's result, I bypasses the pass), Ctrl+F7 cycles L, N, O, P and I, and Shift+F7 toggles A and J. Every mode change is logged, and the reflections card shows a live line with the mode and its counters. It exists to find which part of the pass disturbs the game, not to improve the picture: leave it off for play. Read when the game starts.

keys.name: VfxMaskProbe

menu.iniOnly: a developer probe of the upscaler's mask input, not a player setting

keys.description: Developer probe, ini only: put a constant R8_UNORM mask the size of the picture into the upscaler's mask input, one half full and one half empty. left or right picks the masked half. Comparing two screenshots of the same still scene with it off and on shows whether the backend reads a mask at all: the unmasked half is the noise floor. Anything else reads as off, and nothing is written at all on a frame the probe cannot build a mask for.

keys.name: MipmapBiasAuto
keys.defaultMeans: true for FFXIV, false for other games
keys.description: Follow the upscaling ratio with the mipmap bias (log2 of render width over output width), so there is no number to work out by hand. A MipmapBiasOverride you set always wins and nothing is applied automatically then.

keys.name: MipmapBiasAutoOffset
keys.description: Added to the automatic value. Negative makes textures sharper, positive softer.

keys.name: MipmapBiasObserve

menu.iniOnly: a debug log switch for the bind-time mipmap bias

keys.description: Debug: log every distinct original sampler bias the game uses at each upscaling ratio. No menu control.

keys.name: DynamicMFG
keys.description: Automatic 2X-4X factor selection from the real frame timing, drawn into the XeFG menu row. The slider/InterpolationCount still picks Off/Default. The target is bounded by FramerateLimit.

keys.name: DynamicTargetFPS
keys.description: Target FPS for DynamicMFG, 30 - 500.

keys.name: UnlockMFG
keys.description: Unlocks multi frame generation in Intel's libxess_fg.dll by patching the loaded provider image in memory (the file on disk is never changed). The patches apply when the provider loads: applies after a restart. Turn it off if the provider misbehaves.

keys.name: MaxInterpolatedFrames
keys.description: Interpolated frames reported as the maximum once UnlockMFG is on (N = frames between two rendered frames, menu shows N+1: 1 = 2X ... 7 = 8X). Handed to the provider at swapchain creation: applies after a restart. Values outside 1..7 are ignored.

keys.name: ExtraPacing
keys.description: Spreads every generated frame above 2X out in time instead of presenting the burst back to back. Takes effect once, at XeFG init: needs a game restart.

keys.name: ResetOnUpscalerChange
keys.description: Rebuild the XeFG context when the upscaler is released (quality or NR change) so the provider's pacing history starts clean. Only used by games that isolate NGX shutdown (FFXIV).

keys.name: RenderSizeFromWidthHeight
keys.description: Take the render size from the Width/Height parameters rather than the render subrect. FFXIV only. Leave off unless the render size looks wrong.

keys.name: Style

menu.iniOnly: a theme preference read from the ini when the menu opens

keys.description: Menu style. classic is OptiScaler's own look; ember keeps surfaces neutral and uses the accent colour only to mark state. Anything else reads as classic.

keys.name: FsrMonotonicFrameId

menu.iniOnly: provider-internal FSR frame ID keep-alive, set in the ini only

keys.description: FSR frame generation resets its interpolation history when the frame ID it is given does not rise by exactly 1, and the shared dispatch selector lets that ID jump forward on a skipped frame or fall back after a quality change. On gives FSR its own ID, rising by exactly 1 per dispatch, and hands the provider's callbacks the buffer slot of the dispatch their ID belongs to. Affects the FSR output path only; DLSS-G and XeFG are untouched either way.

keys.name: SkipReleaseSleep

menu.iniOnly: kill switch of the release-path sleep skip

keys.description: Skip the 500 ms pause on upscaler release when the release proved nothing still uses the old upscaler. Off gives exactly the old behaviour.

keys.name: Enabled

menu.iniOnly: diagnostic switch of the generic status.json file beside the DLL

keys.description: Writes status.json next to the DLL (the game folder): a small versioned snapshot for bug reports and tools (versions, feature states, frame-time percentiles, the last writer error). Never holds a path, drive letter, user name or character name. Written atomically by a low-priority background thread, at most once a second on a change plus every 10 s; deleted again when the game exits. Schema in docs/notes/status-json.md.

keys.name: ForcePerfQuality
keys.description: Which quality preset the game is answered with: -1 leave the game's choice alone, 0 Max Performance, 1 Balanced, 2 Max Quality, 3 Ultra Performance, 4 Ultra Quality, 5 DLAA / native.

keys.name: Mode
keys.description: Window mode. off = nothing runs; probe = log only; on = probe plus the border fix and the deferred mode switch. Applies after a game restart. Any other value counts as off.

keys.name: FGOutputHotSwap
keys.description: Live frame-generation output switch: moves the output chain to the new provider while the game runs instead of asking for a restart. It moves between the three DX11-to-DX12 bridge outputs (plain presentation, FSR FG, XeFG), in all six directions, from a run that booted with FSR FG or XeFG; the six directions were verified on the official benchmark (windowed), in runs that booted with FSR FG and in runs that booted with XeFG, not yet in a game session. A chain that fails its first presents is put back to plain presentation and that target is remembered until restart; a session allows a few switches. Off is today's behaviour: the configured output applies on the next start.

keys.name: FGOutputSwitchProbe

menu.iniOnly: developer measurement of the frame-generation libraries' release behaviour

keys.description: Release-model probe: reads the live chain once at the first present - its reference count, the library its present slot lives in, and one test present - and logs one [fg-probe] line per result. It creates and destroys nothing: the measurement that releases a reference runs in the separate probe host under tools/fg-probe, never in the game's process. For a measurement run only.

keys.name: FGOutputSwitchScript

menu.iniOnly: benchmark key: timed output changes, read from the ini only

keys.description: Diagnostic: a timed script of output changes, in seconds from the first bridge present, each entry seconds:target (target none, fsrfg or xefg), comma separated, for example 45:xefg,90:none,135:fsrfg. A step with an unknown target or a missing time is dropped and the rest of the list still runs. Read once, at the first present, and honoured only while FGOutputHotSwap is on; a scripted step does not survive an ini write.

keys.name: FGOutputSwitchFault

menu.iniOnly: benchmark key: one named step fails on purpose, read from the ini only

keys.description: Diagnostic: force one named step of the switch to fail once, so the rollback to plain presentation can be proven in a real process: drain, teardown, create, adopt, replay or probation. The probation fault fires inside a probation only, so it always ends in a rollback to plain; the teardown fault ends the session, because a chain that cannot be freed leaves the window bound. Read once, at the first present, and honoured only while FGOutputHotSwap is on. Empty is no fault.
